risk: Decisions could not be checked or challenged: nothing recorded what the system decided, when, or why
who_is_harmed: Residents whose reports are mis-sorted; managers who must explain decisions
evidence: Before Week 6 no decision was logged anywhere
mitigation: Decision log: every classification and forecast run is written to governance/logs/decisions.csv with reason and rules version

risk: Personal details (phone, ID numbers, emails) could be copied into the decision log
who_is_harmed: Residents who include personal details in reports
evidence: Residents write free text; the log stores a summary of it
mitigation: Summaries are masked and cut to 80 characters before writing; a temporary mask is used until Role 3's mask_personal_info() is merged

risk: Managers may treat forecasts and urgency scores as exact facts
who_is_harmed: Residents in areas or reports that the numbers get wrong
evidence: Forecast is off by about 4 reports a week; classifier got 4 of 30 tricky reports wrong
mitigation: Transparency notes and model cards state accuracy and limits; dashboard shows likely ranges

risk: The decision log has no retention limit, so it keeps growing and holds data longer than needed
evidence: Each full run adds about 4,000 rows; POPIA expects data to be kept no longer than needed
mitigation: Agree a retention period with Role 3 (e.g. 12 months) and delete older rows

risk: Hotspot rankings are not yet recorded in the decision log
who_is_harmed: Residents of areas ranked as quiet
evidence: Only the ranked table is saved, overwritten on every run
mitigation: Log each hotspot run (ranking and cluster count) in the next sprint

risk: Reports written in unsupported languages or wording can be assigned a low default urgency
who_is_harmed: Residents using languages and dialects not represented in keyword rules
evidence: Before changes, synthetic language group category accuracy was 25% and urgency accuracy was 25% across 60 reports
mitigation: Review non-English reports with a fluent speaker; expand phrases using reviewed samples; route uncertain cases for human review

risk: Urgency can be under-scored when elderly, disabled, or pregnant residents are not recognized
who_is_harmed: Elderly, disabled, pregnant residents and caregivers
evidence: Before changes, exact urgency accuracy was 20% (2 of 10) on synthetic vulnerable-group reports
mitigation: Use reviewed vulnerability terms; audit urgency for these groups and retain human escalation for safety-critical reports

risk: Curated translation examples may create false confidence if translations are wrong or coverage is narrow
who_is_harmed: Residents whose phrasing differs from tested samples
evidence: All non-English test IDs are CHECK-marked; translations have not yet been speaker-verified; after metrics use the same 70 curated rows
mitigation: Ask fluent speakers to verify examples; track per-language outcomes and retest variants before relying on scores

risk: Raw report-count hotspot rankings can direct more crews to already busy wards and leave quieter wards waiting longer
who_is_harmed: Residents in wards with fewer reports or barriers to reporting
evidence: Synthetic sample: Old Alexandra has 1,188 reports and Tsutsumani 233; their resolved urgent medians are 23.55 and 44.30 hours
mitigation: Include urgency and reports per verified household count in prioritization; retain a minimum service floor for every ward; review ward-level outcomes

risk: Urgent reports may have persistently longer resolution times in some wards
who_is_harmed: Residents needing urgent services in Tsutsumani, Setswetla, and Far East Bank
evidence: Synthetic sample: urgent medians are 44.30, 37.45, and 36.85 hours respectively, above the 35.33-hour screening threshold
mitigation: Review urgent backlogs and crew allocation by ward; set and monitor a response standard; investigate operational causes before drawing conclusions

risk: Illustrative household assumptions may create misleading reports-per-1,000 rates
who_is_harmed: Residents and managers comparing wards using unsupported denominators
evidence: No census or official household counts were supplied; current ward values are explicit placeholders
mitigation: Replace placeholders with current municipality-approved household estimates matched to ward boundaries; record source and date and recalculate

risk: Personal details written in report text could be stored, shown or sent to an outside LLM
who_is_harmed: Residents who include phone numbers, ID numbers, emails or names in reports
evidence: Scan of 3,994 synthetic reports found 0 matches, but real residents write free text; the optional LLM classifier sends residents' words to an outside company
mitigation: mask_personal_info() in governance/privacy.py masks phones, ID numbers, emails, house numbers and names before reports are logged or sent to an LLM; covered by tests

risk: Masking is pattern-based and can miss personal details in unusual formats, names without a title, or other languages
who_is_harmed: Residents whose details are not recognised and masked
evidence: Tests only cover made-up examples in the formats we listed; no names are recognised unless they follow a title or 'my name is'
mitigation: Do not send unmasked text to an LLM; extend patterns using reviewed samples in each language; keep human review of flagged reports

risk: Health and vulnerability details and exact coordinates could identify a household or expose special personal information
who_is_harmed: Elderly and disabled residents, patients, and households at exact report locations
evidence: Descriptions mention clinics, elderly and disabled residents; every report stores exact latitude and longitude
mitigation: Limit who can see raw reports; show ward-level or rounded locations on shared views; apply stronger protection to special personal information in real data

risk: No retention limit, access control, or way for residents to see and correct their reports
evidence: Data card records no retention period and no dashboard access control; nothing lets a resident request or correct their report
mitigation: Agree a retention period with Role 4 (e.g. 12 months, see R4-04); add access control before real data is used; set up a process for access and correction requests
